1.1: The burden of the woorde of the Lord to Israel by the ministerie of Malachi.
1.2: I have loved you, sayth the Lord: yet yee say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Iaakobs brother, saith the Lord? yet I loved Iaakob,
1.3: And I hated Esau, and made his mountaines wast, and his heritage a wildernes for dragons.
1.4: Though Edom say, wee are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places, yet sayeth the Lord of hostes, they shall build, but I will destroy it, and they shall call them, The border of wickednes, and the people, with whom the Lord is angrie for ever.
1.5: And your eyes shall see it, and yee shall say, The Lord will be magnified upon the border of Israel.
1.6: A sonne honoureth his father, and a servant his master. If then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear, sayth the Lord of hostes unto you, O Priestes, that despise my Name? and yee say, Wherein have we despised thy Name?
1.7: Ye offer vncleane bread upon mine altar, and you say, Wherein have we polluted thee? In that ye say the table of the Lord is not to be regarded.
1.8: And if yee offer the blind for sacrifice, it is not evil: and if ye offer the lame and sick, it is not evil: offer it now unto thy prince: will he be content with thee, or accept thy person, saieth the Lord of hostes?
1.9: And now, I pray you, pray before God, that he may have mercie upon us: this hath been by your meanes: will hee regard your persons, sayth the Lord of hostes?
1.10: Who is there even among you, that would shut the doores? and kindle not fire on mine altar in vain, I have no pleasure in you, sayeth the Lord of hostes, neither will I accept an offering at your hand.
1.11: For from the rising of the sunne unto the going down of the same, my Name is great among the Gentiles, and in every place incense shalbe offred unto my Name, and a pure offering: for my Name is great among the heathen, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
1.12: But ye have polluted it, in that ye say, The table of the Lord is polluted and the fruit thereof, even his meat is not to be regarded.
1.13: Ye said also, Behold, it is a wearines, and ye have snuffed at it, sayth the Lord of hostes, and ye offred that which was torn, and the lame and the sick: thus yee offred an offring: should I accept this of your hand, sayth the Lord?
1.14: But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto ye Lord a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, sayth the Lord of hostes, and my Name is terrible among the heathen.

2.1: And now, O ye Priests, this commandement is for you.
2.2: If yee will not hear it, nor consider it in your heart, to give glory unto my Name, sayth the Lord of hostes, I will even send a curse upon you, and will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them alreadie, because yee doe not consider it in your heart.
2.3: Behold, I wil corrupt your seed, and cast dongue upon your faces, even the dongue of your solemn feastes, and you shall be like unto it.
2.4: And yee shall know, that I have sent this commandement unto you, that my covenant, which I made with Levi, might stand, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
2.5: My covenant was with him of life and peace, and I gave him fear, and he feared mee, and was afraid before my Name.
2.6: The law of trueth was in his mouth, and there was no iniquitie found in his lippes: hee walked with me in peace and equitie, and did turn many away from iniquitie.
2.7: For the Priestes lippes should preserve knowledge, and they should seek the Law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hostes.
2.8: But yee are gone out of the way: yee have caused many to fall by the Law: yee have broken the covenant of Levi, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
2.9: Therefore have I also made you to be despised, and vile before all the people, because yee kept not my wayes, but have been partial in the Law.
2.10: Have we not all one father? hath not one God made us? why doe we transgress every one against his brother, and break the covenant of our fathers?
2.11: Judah hath transgressed, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem: for Judah hath defiled the holiness of the Lord, which hee loved, and hath maried the daughter of a strange God.
2.12: The Lord will cut off the man that doeth this: both the master and the seruaunt out of the Tabernacle of Iaacob, and him that offereth an offering unto the Lord of hostes.
2.13: And this have ye done again, and covered the altar of the Lord with teares, with weeping and with mourning: because the offering is no more regarded, neither received acceptably at your handes.
2.14: Yet yee say, Wherein? Because the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast transgressed: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.
2.15: And did not hee make one? yet had hee abundance of spirit: and wherefore one? because he sought a godly seed: therefore keep your selves in your spirit, and let none trespass against the wife of his youth.
2.16: If thou hatest her, put her away, sayeth the Lord God of Israel, yet he covereth the iniurie under his garment, saieth the Lord of hosts: therefore keep your selves in your spirit, and transgress not.
2.17: Yee have wearied the Lord with your woordes: yet yee say, Wherein have we wearied him? When ye say, Every one that doeth evil, is good in the sight of the Lord, and he deliteth in them. Or where is the God of iudgement?

3.1: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord whom ye seek, shall speedely come to his Temple: even the messenger of the covenant whom ye desire: behold, he shall come, sayth the Lord of hostes.
3.2: But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall endure, when he appeareth? for he is like a purging fire, and like fullers sop.
3.3: And he shall sit down to try and fine the silver: he shall even fine the sonnes of Levi and purifie them as gold and silver, that they may bring offerings unto the Lord in righteousness.
3.4: Then shall the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem be acceptable unto the Lord, as in old time and in the yeeres afore.
3.5: And I will come neere to you to iudgement, and I will be a swift witness against the southsayers, and against the adulterers, and against false swearers, and against those that wrongfully keep back the hirelings wages, and vex the widow, and the fatherless, and oppress the stranger, and fear not me, sayth the Lord of hostes.
3.6: For I am the Lord: I change not, and ye sonnes of Iaakob are not consumed.
3.7: From the dayes of your fathers, ye are gone away from mine ordinances, and have not kept them: return unto me, and I will return unto you, saith the Lord of hostes: but ye said, Wherein shall we return?
3.8: Will a man spoyle his gods? yet have ye spoyled me: but ye say, Wherein have we spoyled thee? In tithes, and offerings.
3.9: Ye are cursed with a curse: for ye have spoyled me, even this whole nation.
3.10: Bring ye all the tythes into the storehouse that there may be meat in mine House, and prove me now herewith, sayeth the Lord of hostes, if I will not open the windowes of heaven unto you, and powre you out a blessing without measure.
3.11: And I will rebuke the deuourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruit of your ground, neither shall your vine be baren in the field, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
3.12: And all nations shall call you blessed: for ye shall be a pleasant land, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
3.13: Your wordes have been stout against me, sayeth the Lord: yet ye say, What have we spoken against thee?
3.14: Ye have said, It is in vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his commandement, and that we walked humbly before the Lord of hostes?
3.15: Therefore wee count the proud blessed: even they that work wickedness, are set up, and they that tempt God, yea, they are delivered.
3.16: Then spake they that feared the Lord, every one to his neighbour, and the Lord hearkened and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his Name.
3.17: And they shall be to me, sayeth the Lord of hostes, in that day that I shall do this, for a flock, and I will spare them, as a man spareth his own sonne that serveth him.
3.18: Then shall you return, and discern between the righteous and wicked, between him that serveth God, and him that serveth him not.

4.1: For behold, the day cometh that shall burn as an oven, and all the proud, yea, and all that doe wickedly, shall be stubble, and the day that cometh, shall burn them up, sayeth the Lord of hostes, and shall leave them neither root nor branch.
4.2: But unto you that fear my Name, shall the sunne of righteousness arise, and health shall be under his wings, and ye shall goe forth, and grow up as fat calves.
4.3: And ye shall tread down the wicked: for they shall be dust under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall doe this, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
4.4: Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel with the statutes and iudgements.
4.5: Behold, I will send you Eliiah the Prophet before the coming of the great and fearefull day of the Lord.
4.6: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with cursing.

39:1:2: Which declareth their great ingratitude that did not acknowledge this love, which was so evident, in that he chose Abraham from out of all the world, and next chose Jacob the younger brother of whom they came, and left Esau the elder.
39:1:3: For beside here the signs of mine hatred appeared even when he was made servant unto his younger brother, being yet in his mother’s belly, and also afterward in that he was put from his birthright, yet even now before your eyes the signs hereof are evident, in that that his country lieth waste and he shall never return to inhabit.
Whereas ye my people, whom the enemy hated more than them, are by my grace and love toward you delivered, read Rom. 9:13.
39:1:6: He noteth their gross hypocrisy, which would not see their faults, but most impudently covered them, and so were blind guides.

Besides the rest of the people he condemneth the Priests chiefly, because they should have reproved others for their hypocrisy, and obstinacy against God, and not have hardened them by their example to greater evils.
39:1:7: Ye receive all manner offerings for your own greediness, and do not examine whether they be according to my Law, or no.
Not that they said thus, but by their doings they declared no less.
39:1:8: You make it no fault: whereby he condemneth them, that think it sufficient to serve God partly as he hath commanded, and partly after man’s fantasy: and so come not to the pureness of religion, which he requireth, and therefore in reproach he showeth them that a mortal man would not be content to be so served.
39:1:9: He derideth the Priests who bare the people in hand that they prayed for them, and showeth that they were the occasion, that these evils came upon the people.
Will God consider your office and state, seeing you are so covetous and wicked?
39:1:10: Because the Levites who kept the doors did not try whether the sacrifices that came in, were according to the Law, God wisheth that they would rather shut the doors, than to receive such as were not perfect.
39:1:11: God showeth that their ingratitude, and neglect of his true service shall be the cause of the calling of the Gentiles: and here the Prophet that was under the Law, framed his words to the capacity of the people, and by the altar and sacrifice he meaneth the spiritual service of God, which should be under the Gospel, when an end should be made to all these legal ceremonies by Christ’s only sacrifice.
39:1:12: Both the Priests and the people were infected with this error, that they passed not what was offered: for they thought that God was as well content with the lean, as with the fat: but in the mean season they showed not that obedience to God, which he required, and so committed both impiety, and also showed their contempt of God, and covetousness.
39:1:13: The Priests and people were both weary with serving God, and passed not what manner of sacrifice and service they gave to God: for that which was least profitable, was thought good enough for the Lord.
39:1:14: That is, hath ability to serve the Lord according to his word, and yet will serve him according to his covetous mind.
39:2:1: He speaketh unto them chiefly, but under them he containeth the people also.
39:2:2: To serve me according to my word.
That is, the abundance of God’s benefits.
39:2:3: Your seed sown shall come to no profit.
You boast of your holiness, sacrifices and feasts, but they shall turn to your shame and be as vile as dung.
39:2:4: The Priests objected against the Prophet that he could not reprove them, but he must speak against the Priesthood, and the office established of God by promise, but he showeth that the office is nothing slandered, when these villains and dung are called by their own names.
39:2:5: He served me and set forth my glory with all humilitude and submission.

He showeth what were the two conditions of the covenant made with the tribe of Levi on God’s part, that he would give them long life and felicity, and on their part, that they should faithfully serve him according to his word.
I prescribed Levi a certain Law to serve me.
39:2:6: He showeth that the Priests ought to have knowledge to instruct others in the word of the Lord.
39:2:7: He is as the treasure house of God’s word, and ought to give to everyone according to their necessity, and not to reserve it for himself.
Showing that whosoever doth not declare God’s will, is not his messenger, and Priest.
39:2:10: The Prophet accuseth the ingratitude of the Jews toward God and man: for seeing they were all born of one father Abraham, and God had elected them to be his holy people, they ought neither to offend God nor their brethren.
Whereby they had bound themselves to God to be an holy people.
39:2:11: They have joined themselves in marriage with them that are of another religion.
39:2:13: Yet cause the people to lament, because that God doth not regard their sacrifices, so that they seem to sacrifice in vain.
39:2:14: She that was joined to thee by a solemn covenant, and by the invocation of God’s name.
As the one half of thyself.
This is another fault, whereof he accuseth them, that is, that they broke the laws of marriage.
39:2:15: Did not God make man and woman as one flesh and not many?
Contain yourselves within your bounds, and be sober in mind, and bridle your affections.
Such as should be born in lawful and moderate marriage, wherein is no excess of lusts.
By his power and virtue he could have made many women for one man.
39:2:16: He thinketh it sufficient to keep his wife still, albeit he take others, and so as it were covereth his fault.
Not that he doth allow divorcement, but of two faults he showeth, which is the less.
39:2:17: Thus they blasphemed God in condemning his power and justice, because he judged not according to their fantasies.
Ye murmur against God, because he heard not you as soon as ye called.
In thinking that God favored the wicked, and hath no respect to them that serve him.
39:3:1: This is meant of John Baptist, as Christ expoundeth it, Luke 7:27.

That is, Christ, by whom the covenant was made and ratified, who is called the Angel or messenger of the covenant, because he reconcileth us to his father and is Lord or king, because he hath the government of his Church.
39:3:2: He showeth that the hypocrites which wish so much for the Lord’s coming will not abide when he draweth near: for he will consume them, and purge his and make them clean.
39:3:3: He beginneth at the Priests that they might be lights, and shine unto others.
39:3:6: They murmured against God, because they saw not his help ever present to defend them: and therefore he accuseth them of ingratitude, and showeth that in that they are not daily consumed, it is a token, that he doth still defend them, and so his mercy toward them never changeth.
39:3:8: There are none of the heathen so barbarous, that will defraud their gods of their honor, or deal deceitfully with them.
Whereby the service of God should have been maintained, and the Priests and the poor relieved.
39:3:10: Not having respect how much ye need, but I will give you in all abundance: so that ye shall lack place to put my blessings in.
39:3:11: Meaning, the caterpillar, and whatsoever destroyeth corn and fruits.
39:3:13: The Prophet condemneth them of double blasphemy against God: first, in that they said that God had no respect to them that served him, and next, that the wicked were more in his favor than the godly.
39:3:15: They are not only preferred to honor, but also delivered from dangers.
39:3:16: After these admonitions of the Prophet, some were lively touched, and encouraged others to fear God.
Both because the thing was strange that some turned to God in that great and universal corruption, and also that this might be an example of God’s mercies to all penitent sinners.
39:3:17: That is, forgive their sins, and govern them with my Spirit.
When I shall restore my Church according to my promise, they shall be as mine own proper goods.
39:4:1: He prophesieth of God’s judgments against the wicked, who would not receive Christ, when as God should send him for the restoration of his Church.
39:4:2: Ye shall be set at liberty, and increase in the joy of the Spirit, 2 Cor. 3:17.

Meaning, Christ, who with his wings or beams of his grace should lighten and comfort his Church, Eph. 5:14, and he is called the sun of righteousness, because in himself he hath all perfection and also the justice of the Father dwelleth in him: whereby he regenerateth us unto righteousness, cleanseth us from the filth of this world, and reformeth us to the image of God.
39:4:4: Because the time was come that the Jews should be destitute of Prophets until the time of Christ, because they should with more fervent minds desire his coming, the Prophet exhorteth them to exercise themselves diligently in studying the Law of Moses in the mean season, whereby they might continue in the true religion, and also be armed against all tentations.
39:4:5: This Christ expoundeth of John Baptist, Matt. 11:13, 14, who both for his zeal, and restoring of religion, is aptly compared to Elijah.
Which as it is true for the wicked, so doth it waken the godly, and call them to repentance.
39:4:6: He showeth wherein John’s office should stand: in the turning of men to God, and joining the father and children in one voice of faith: so that the father shall turn to the religion of his son which is converted to Christ, and the son shall embrace the faith of the true fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The second point of his office was to denounce God’s judgments against them that would not receive Christ.
